validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED, high confidence. The Wafra->BS-171 gas export pipeline is a real Kuwait Oil Company (KOC) project, corroborated by multiple fully independent origins that do NOT trace to GEM: (1) Global Flow Control 'Combined Group Wins $42M Gas Pipeline Project for Wafra in Kuwait' (verified: contains Wafra, Kuwait, 42); (2) Zawya 'CGC emerges lowest bidder for Kuwait gas pipeline project' (verified: contains Wafra, 65, KOC) describing a 65 km export pipeline from Wafra Joint Operations to KOC's gas booster station, KD12.7m/$42m, 30-month completion, EPC scope; (3) DMS Universe project listing 'KOC - Gas Export Pipeline from Wafra Joint Operations to BS-171' (verified: Wafra, 65, BS-171); (4) Al-Anba Arabic article (verified: الوفرة, 65); (5) Arab News (2022-01-10) on KGOC / Saudi Arabian Chevron exporting spare gas from Wafra Joint Operations. So this is not a GEM-only / hallucinated entity. CLASSIFICATION: gas transmission is correct - it is a gas EXPORT pipeline carrying spare/associated gas from the Wafra Joint Operations (the partitioned-neutral-zone heavy-oil operation jointly run by Kuwait Gulf Oil Co. and Saudi Arabian Chevron) to KOC's gas booster station BS-171, which processes dry/conditioned export gas; not an NGL line, not a gathering line. ATTRIBUTION CAVEATS (not blocking but should be corrected): (a) GEM Owner = 'Kuwait Petroleum Corp 100%' but every source names the project owner/client as Kuwait Oil Company (KOC), KPC's upstream subsidiary - KOC is the more precise owner/operator. (b) GEM End State/Province = 'Al Jahra Governorate' but independent sources (DMS Universe, KOC project descriptions, the gem.wiki text itself) place BS-171 / Booster Station 171 in Al Ahmadi Governorate / West Kuwait, NOT Al Jahra. SPECS: length 65 km = high (multiple independent agree); cost $42m / KD12.7m = high (Zawya + Global Flow Control); ProposalYear 2022 = high (Arab News Jan 2022 + 2022 bidding); diameter 20 in = medium (only the Arabic Al-Anba source carries a diameter, no English corroboration found); StartYear1 2028 = medium/inferred (derived from ~30-month completion off a 2025 award, not a stated commissioning date). Note: this row sits in the Saudi gas roster but is physically a Kuwait/Neutral-Zone pipeline owned by a Kuwaiti operator - geographically a Kuwait asset, though the feed (Wafra JO) is jointly Saudi/Kuwaiti, so its placement in the Saudi sweep is defensible. No duplicate found in the 65-row Saudi gas roster.

validity.recommendation: change End State/Province from 'Al Jahra Governorate' to 'Al Ahmadi Governorate'; consider changing Owner from 'Kuwait Petroleum Corp' to 'Kuwait Oil Company (KOC)'
validity.researcher_notes: Two attribution errors. (1) END GOVERNORATE: GEM has BS-171 in 'Al Jahra Governorate', but BS-171 / Booster Station 171 is consistently described as being in Al Ahmadi Governorate / West Kuwait by independent sources (DMS Universe 'KOC - West Kuwait Booster Station 171 (BS-171)', verified: contains BS-171, West Kuwait), and KOC's West Kuwait BS-171 ties into the Mina Al Ahmadi gas system. Al Jahra appears to be an error. (2) OWNER: GEM has 'Kuwait Petroleum Corp 100%'; the project owner/client across all sources is Kuwait Oil Company (KOC), the KPC upstream subsidiary that owns and operates Kuwait's oil/gas pipelines and BS-171. KPC is the parent holding company; KOC is the actual asset owner/operator. Recommend listing KOC for precision (KPC is not strictly wrong as ultimate parent, so this is a softer fix than the governorate).

summary: P5854 Wafra-Station 171 gas pipeline EXISTS (real KOC 65 km Wafra JO->BS-171 export line, $42M CGCC, high confidence) and is correctly classified as gas transmission; attribution concern: end governorate is Al Ahmadi not Al Jahra, and owner is KOC not KPC; no duplicate in Saudi roster.
